title: Rewrite useTanStackTableDevtools to split-form createRenderEffect
description:
## Why
solid-table-devtools/src/useTanStackTableDevtools.ts uses the 1-arg createRenderEffect with nested onCleanup — Solid 2 requires the split (compute, effectFn) signature with the effect half returning its cleanup. Needed under BOTH devtools-epic outcomes (island or fallback).

## What (design D21)
createRenderEffect(
  () => ((options?.enabled ?? true) && table ? table : undefined),   // tracked: props reads live here
  (target) => { if (!target) return; const cleanup = upsertTableDevtoolsTarget({ table: target }); return () => cleanup?.() },
)
Keep createRenderEffect (not createEffect) so devtools registration precedes user effects. Prefer returned-cleanup over onCleanup (the documented 2.0 contract). Size S.
design: Plan refs: D21. Blocked by the createEffect-timing spike.
acceptance_criteria: Hook registers/unregisters correctly under Solid 2 (unit test); enabled-toggle reactivity preserved.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by rcv.7 NO-GO + gau.4 fallback: solid-table-devtools stays a Solid-1-only package (peers <2.0.0), and under Solid 1 the two-arg split form is actively WRONG — Solid 1's createRenderEffect(fn, value) treats arg 2 as the initial prev value, so the effect half would never run and devtools registration would silently vanish. The current 1-arg + onCleanup form is correct for the package's actual runtime. The D21 split-form recipe (compute reads options?.enabled/table; braced effect half returns the upsert cleanup) transfers to table-v3p.2 (full devtools Solid 2 migration when upstream ships). The bead's 'needed under BOTH outcomes' premise assumed the island outcome kept the hook in the app's Solid 2 graph — dead with the island.

title: Add the 8 new Solid-2 semantic tests (D25)
description:
## Why
The type system catches none of the Solid-2 semantic changes. These tests are the migration's real safety net and the executable contract with Solid's beta churn.

## What (design D25.1-8)
1. Microtask coalescing: N writes -> exactly one effect run after one flush().
2. Consecutive functional updates: two atom.set(old=>...) in one tick — second sees the first (guards columnResizingFeature.utils.ts:222).
3. Imperative read-your-writes: table.setPageSize(50); expect(table.atoms.pagination.get().pageSize).toBe(50) with NO flush() — the executable spec for settle-on-read.
4. Stale-window pin: a tracked read inside a memo during the pending window returns the committed value and converges after flush() — pins semantics so a Solid beta bump fails loudly.
5. ownedWrite silence: spy console.warn around construction + a table.setX() inside a createEffect -> zero warnings; PLUS a bounded-effect-run infinite-loop tripwire (replaces the protection ownedWrite:true forfeits).
6. Subscribe contract: first emission synchronous; no duplicate first emission after first flush; unsubscribe idempotent; owner disposal stops delivery.
7. Context: useTableContext/useCellContext/useHeaderContext outside providers throw OUR messages, not ContextNotFoundError.
8. Two-way external-atom sync under deferral: interleave externalAtom.set(A) and table.setRowSelection(B) in one tick -> single converged winner on both sides, no notification loop (guards constructTable.ts:91-104, whose syncExternal guard assumed synchronous delivery).
Size L.
design: Plan refs: D25. Blocked by reactivity + createTable rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 tests exist, green, and are named/commented so their contract role is obvious; tests 3-4 explicitly reference the settle-on-read decision.
notes: ADD to the D25 set (from rcv.3 findings): (a) batching-regression measurement for the D14 flush-around-write recipe — N state updates in one event handler vs Solid-1 baseline (N global drains vs one coalesced update); if material, adopt 65n.3's APPLY-phase-writes fallback. (b) same-tick swallow regression test: reactive props change + table.setOptions in ONE tick must not lose the props change (the exact hazard rcv.3(c) found). (c) tearing pin: derived atoms created via createReadonlyAtom must NOT tear vs their base atom in the pending window (rcv.1(b)).

All 8 D25 tests + rcv.3 additions green (D25.7 in rendering.test.tsx with jsdom + throw-site constraint; rcv.3(b) swallow regression in options-store.smoke.test.ts; tearing pin folded into D25.4). Suite total 146/146; tsc 0; lint clean. MEASUREMENT rcv.3(a): 50 setOptions with flush-both-sides = 7.67ms (~0.15ms/write) vs 50 coalesced state writes = 2.16ms — ~3.5x relative, negligible absolute; DECISION: keep D14 recipe, APPLY-phase fallback NOT adopted. title: Migrate the 5 unit-test files to Solid 2 timing + testing-library 1.0
description:
## Why
1,172 lines of tests assert exact synchronous effect-run counts; Solid 2 defers everything to microtask. The batch() import disappears. testing-library moves to 1.0.0-beta.2.

## What (design D23/D24)
- New shared harness tests/utils/reactive.ts: createEffectTestRoot (currently duplicated in 3 files), settle() = flush(), settleAsync() = await Promise.resolve() then flush() (for anything downstream of the schedule() binding — e.g. table_autoResetPageIndex now takes two turns).
- Mechanical discipline: every createRoot(setup) creating effects gets flush() before first assertion; every mutation followed by an EFFECT-COUNT assertion gets flush(); mutations followed by VALUE assertions via table APIs stay flush-free IFF settle-on-read shipped (they become its regression tests).
- adapterReactivity.test.ts:246-269: rewrite the batch()-of-5-setters block as five bare setters + one flush(); expected outcome (exactly 2 snapshots) UNCHANGED — it now proves microtask coalescing.
- rendering.test.tsx: apply the fireEvent flush rules from the testing-library spike.
- REVIEW RULE (risk R10): every inserted flush() must be justified as effect-count (legitimate) vs value-assertion (suspicious — must trace to a settle-on-read design decision), so the rewrite cannot mask a real staleness regression.
Size L.
design: Plan refs: D23, D24, R10. Blocked by reactivity + createTable rewrites and the testing-library spike.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 files green under Solid 2; zero unexplained flush() insertions per the review rule; harness shared (no duplicated helpers).
notes:
MIGRATION RULES validated by table-rcv.5 (GO): (R1) EVERY bare fireEvent.* gets settle() immediately after — NOT cosmetic: un-flushed read-modify-write handlers COLLAPSE (3 clicks => 1, handler reads [0,0,0]); 5 sites in rendering.test.tsx (lines ~141,144,147,183,223). (R2) render() needs NO settling (fully sync — @solidjs/web's render flushes internally). (R3) expect(() => render(...)).toThrow() unchanged (throws synchronously; lines 447/451/455). (R4) KEEP afterEach(() => cleanup()) at line 12 + inline cleanups — auto-cleanup needs a GLOBAL afterEach and repo runs vitest globals:false (silent no-op, same as 0.8.10). (R5) import line unchanged; ADD import { flush } from 'solid-js' or use the shared harness. (R6) the other 4 unit files don't import the testing library at all.
HARNESS (D23): settle() { flush() } — sync, idempotent, safe when idle; settleAsync() { flush(); await Promise.resolve(); flush() }; clickAndSettle(el) recommended codemod target. waitFor also settles (escape hatch).
HAZARDS: flush() THROWS inside onSettled/createTrackedEffect ('not reentrant there') — settle() must never be called from those callbacks. table.Subscribe/@tanstack/store bridge path (rendering.test.tsx:217-230) UNTESTED by the spike — confirm one settle() suffices (or settleAsync) on first real port. A throwing render() leaks its container div into document.body (pre-existing). API: renderDirective now throws; renderRef new; nothing the repo uses renamed.
close_reason: Landed on solid-2-adapter-core. 138/138 tests green (27 unit + 111 spike); tsc 0 errors; eslint clean; all five nx gates green. Harness at tests/utils/reactive.ts. Key findings: one-arg createEffect is GONE (types make following code unreachable) — all captors converted to two-arg braced form; per-update assertions need settle() between writes (coalescing); externalAtom (raw store atom) reads after table writes need settle() — the table->external sync rides a Solid effect; Subscribe/store-bridge needs exactly one settle (rcv.5 caveat resolved). Every inserted flush justified per R10: effect-count or raw-read; table-API value reads kept flush-free as D10-A regression tests.

title: Rewrite src/createTable.ts (options sync without createComputed, owner acquisition)
description:
## Why
createComputed is removed. The options-sync loop is the single highest-risk change: table.options freshness is what makes getRowModel() correct (tableMemo re-reads table.options.data on every call), and a deferred sync would make row models one tick stale.

## What (design D13/D14/D16/D17)
- PREFERRED (if the writable-memo spike passes): function-form createSignal writable memo as the options store — options become pull-based, always current on read; hook: createWritableAtom special-cases debugName === 'table/optionsStore'. This supersedes the effect-based sync and removes the staleness class at the root.
- OTHERWISE: split-form createRenderEffect (runs in the render queue BEFORE user effects — the direct analogue of Svelte's $effect.pre at createTable.svelte.ts:87-103): tracked half resolves options via flatMerge + touches every tableOptions.state key (for..in + void read — nested keys are getter-backed and otherwise never tracked); effect half does untrack(() => table.setOptions(prev => mergeObjects(prev, next))).
- Owner: getOwner() ?? createOwner() + dev-mode console.warn when null (in 2.0 runWithOwner(null) MEANS detach, so the old getOwner()! failure becomes a silent leak instead of a crash).
- Keep onCleanup(() => reactivity.unmount?.()), table.Subscribe, table.FlexRender unchanged.
Size L.
design: Plan refs: D13, D14, D16, D17. Blocked by the writable-memo spike, the merge vendoring, and the reactivity rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Options pushed before render reads in the same flush (no one-frame-stale row models — regression test); controlled-state tests green; dev warning fires when constructed outside a root; micro-benchmark from the merge issue stays flat.
notes: D14 recipe VALIDATED by table-rcv.3 (read its notes for the three hazards before implementing): optionsStore = createSignal(prev => mergeObjects(prev, mergedOptions()), { name: 'table/optionsStore', ownedWrite: true }) — function form takes TWO args (fn, options), NO initialValue. get(): if (!getObserver()) flush(); return raw(). set(u): flush(); setRaw(u); flush() — flush on BOTH sides is mandatory (leading alone still permanently swallows a same-tick dep change). DELETE the createComputed push-sync outright (no re-push, no per-state-key touch loop needed). createWritableAtom special-cases debugName==='table/optionsStore' (svelte precedent reactivity.svelte.ts:112). mergeObjects comes from 65n.1's vendored module — NEVER @solidjs/web mergeProps. Owner: getOwner() ?? createOwner() + dev warning (D17). FALLBACK if the flush-around-write batching regression is material (N setOptions in one handler = N global drains): route imperative writes through an effect APPLY phase (needs no ownedWrite, cannot swallow) at the cost of one scheduling hop — measurement owed with 65n.6.

title: Rewrite src/reactivity.ts for Solid 2 (subscribe bridge, batch, settle-on-read)
description:
## Why
observable() and batch are removed in Solid 2; all updates defer to microtask. reactivity.ts is the adapter's bridge to table-core's TableReactivityBindings contract and every removed API lives here.

## What (design D4-D12; ~93 -> ~150 lines)
- subscribe bridge: nested createRoot under the table's owner + two-arg createEffect(read, emit). Manual eager first emission with an emitted+Object.is dedup guard (do NOT rely on {defer} — a write between subscribe() and first flush would be swallowed). Normalize Observer-object vs bare-callback subscribers (observerToCallback, cf. svelte reactivity.svelte.ts:11-17). Idempotent unsubscribe via a local disposed flag (2.0 nested roots are parent-owned, so owner disposal + explicit unsubscribe = double-dispose reachable; adapterReactivity.test.ts:34-77 asserts exactly-once).
- batch binding: identity (fn => fn()) — Solid 2 auto-batches; NOT fn => {fn(); flush()} (runs user effects mid-update, half-settles the graph).
- schedule: keep queueMicrotask (distinct tick; downstream resets now take two microtask turns).
- settle-on-imperative-read (D10-A): every atom get() calls flush() when getObserver()===null && getOwner()===null and not already settling. Preserves read-your-writes for imperative callers. Gate on the empty-queue flush() cost from the pending-write spike; fallback D10-B (settle only when an adapter write is pending) if expensive.
- functional updates keep delegating to Solid's setter (pending-prev guarantee; guards columnResizingFeature.utils.ts:222-238).
- ownedWrite: true on all adapter-created writable atoms (core legitimately writes from reactive scopes); the lost loop-tripwire is compensated by a bounded-effect-run test.
- Memo/signal option mapping stays 1:1 ({equals: compare, name: debugName}); do NOT adopt {lazy}/{unobserved} in this migration.
- Keep createOptionsStore:true and wrapExternalAtoms:true (unless the spike forces the A2 store-bridge fallback, which flips wrapExternalAtoms to false and replaces this design).
Size L.
design: Plan refs: D4-D12. Blocked by pending-write + createEffect spikes and the integration branch.
acceptance_criteria: All TableReactivityBindings implemented per D4-D12; existing reactivity tests (migrated) green; new semantic tests green; no ownedWrite dev warnings during construction + setX-from-effect.
notes: IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS locked by spikes (read table-rcv.1/.2 notes in full first): (1) createReadonlyAtom MUST create memos INSIDE the table owner — unowned memos tear against pending values (rcv.1(b)); (2) subscribe bridge: DEFAULT (non-deferred) two-arg createEffect in nested createRoot + manual eager first emission + emitted&&Object.is dedup — guard is load-bearing; do NOT use {defer} (never-changing source => subscriber never initialised) or {sync} (not a scheduling mode); (3) effect half MUST be a braced block returning undefined — any other non-function return PERMANENTLY HALTS reactivity (REACTIVITY_HALTED); type the emit wrapper (v:T)=>void (see table-65n.9); (4) settle-on-read: get() = if (getObserver()===null) flush(); untracked read — knowingly INERT inside reactive scopes (computes already read pending; adapter code reading back its own write inside an effect must use latest()); (5) batch binding = identity CONFIRMED (flush(fn) is NOT a settling scope; no per-write mode exists); (6) ownedWrite:true on every adapter writable atom; map debugName -> Solid option `name`; (7) nested-root dispose is parent-owned + double-dispose safe => D6 unsubscribe needs no extra guards. title: Vendor merge-objects (mergeProps replacement) and swap in at all 5 sites
description:
## Why
Solid 2 renames mergeProps to merge AND changes semantics: undefined now OVERRIDES instead of being skipped. table_mergeOptions calls our mergeOptions binding as mergeOptions(table.options, newOptions) where table.options carries every feature default — so any present-but-undefined user key (the ubiquitous wrapper pattern { onSortingChange: props.onSortingChange } with an optional prop) would silently erase the default makeStateUpdater handler and break that state slice. A stripUndefined pre-pass is not viable (it must read every getter eagerly, destroying getter-preservation).

## What
Copy packages/svelte-table/src/merge-objects.ts (getter-preserving, undefined-skipping; itself lifted from Solid 1 source) to packages/solid-table/src/merge-objects.ts. Swap in at: createTable.ts:68, :75, :81 (the mergeOptions binding), :102, and createTableHook.tsx:818. Also adopt flatMerge in the options-sync loop (quadratic getter-chain fix, cf. Svelte PR #6266). Solid-version-agnostic — can be built and tested before the flip. Size M.

## Review trap
mergeProps still exists in @solidjs/web WITH THE NEW SEMANTICS — importing it from there is the silent-regression trap; forbid it in review.
design: Plan refs: D15, D16, R2-risk.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 sites use vendored mergeObjects; unit tests prove (a) {onSortingChange: undefined} does NOT disable sorting, (b) getters survive merging un-evaluated, (c) flatMerge caps getter-chain depth (200-push micro-benchmark: table.options.data read time stays flat).
notes:
DONE — all 5 gates green: test:lib (27 tests, 21 pre-existing + 6 new), test:types, test:eslint, build, test:build (publint --strict; only pre-existing repository.url suggestion). Sites swapped: createTable.ts:63/:70/:76/:102 + createTableHook.tsx:819; solid-js mergeProps imports removed; grep-verified NO mergeProps/merge import from solid-js or @solidjs/web anywhere in solid-table src. merge-objects.ts is internal (not re-exported), matching svelte-table. New files: src/merge-objects.ts, tests/unit/mergeObjects.test.ts.
DELIBERATE DEVIATION (review me): a byte-identical svelte copy FAILS acceptance (a). svelte's mergeObjects defines own enumerable getters even for all-undefined keys, and constructTable.ts:82's spread then copies onSortingChange:undefined over the feature default. Verified on the UNTOUCHED tree that Solid 1's own mergeProps has the same hole — TODAY {onSortingChange: undefined} makes setSorting a SILENT NO-OP. The vendored copy adds an isKeyDefined guard: skip a key when every source's descriptor is a plain data property holding undefined; getters and function sources always count defined (preserves laziness; matches Solid-1 intent). Net: behavior-preserving EXCEPT it FIXES that pre-existing bug — this change is a genuine beta bugfix, not just Solid-2 prep.
flatMerge: vendored + unit-tested (200-merge chain: mergeObjects = 200 getter hops/read, flatMerge = plain data property) but NOT adopted at sites :76/:102 — adoption needs the eager-resolution restructure and silently coarsens reactivity granularity; follow-up: table-65n.8. title: Spike: function-form createSignal writable memo as the options store
description:
## Why
Solid 2's function-form createSignal(prev => compute) is a writable memo. If an imperative write persists until the next dependency change and prev is the last written value, the options store becomes PULL-BASED: table.options is always current on read with no effect, no scheduling, no ownedWrite write-from-effect, and no read-after-write staleness. This is the only design that removes the options-staleness bug class at the root (D14) rather than compensating for it (D13 createRenderEffect + D10 settle-on-read).

## What
Spike: create a function-form signal wrapping merged options; (a) write imperatively via set() — does the value persist until a dependency changes? (b) after a dependency change, is prev the last written value or the last computed value? (c) interleave imperative writes and dependency changes in one tick.

## Outcome
If it passes: D14 supersedes D13 as the options-sync design and materially de-risks D10. Implementation hook: createWritableAtom special-cases debugName === 'table/optionsStore' (same hook the Svelte adapter uses at reactivity.svelte.ts:112). Keep as a permanent contract test.
design: Plan refs: D13, D14, S3. Blocks the createTable.ts rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Questions (a)-(c) answered with test evidence; D14-vs-D13 decision recorded; spike preserved as permanent contract test.
notes:
SPIKE ANSWERS (writable-memo-options-store.spike.test.ts, all green incl. 8-test recipe block; durable copy: .claude/solid2-spikes/). API CORRECTIONS: function form is createSignal(fn, options) — TWO args, NO initialValue (the JSDoc advertising three is wrong); Solid's option is `name` (map our TableAtomOptions.debugName to it).
(a) Committed writes persist indefinitely (identity-stable across unrelated flushes; compute never re-runs); a later-tick dep change replaces them. BUT the D14 premise "always current on read" is FALSE for UNOWNED reads (event handlers / imperative API — exactly how table.options is consumed): stale within the tick for BOTH writes and dep changes (dev.js read() returns _pendingValue only when context non-null; pulls only when context && tracking). TRACKED reads are current and do pull. Non-lazy writable memo computes EAGERLY at creation; {lazy:true} defers to first read.
(b) prev on recompute = last COMMITTED value BY IDENTITY (= the last written object whenever a write committed since the previous compute). table.setOptions(prev => merge(prev, ...)) merge-into-prev survives intact.
(c) Same-tick interleaving deterministic + order-independent: the manual write wins the tick and the memo does NOT recompute that tick. HAZARD: the swallowed same-tick dep change is PERMANENTLY LOST (REACTIVE_MANUAL_WRITE unschedules; insertIntoHeap early-returns) — the memo never catches up to that dep value; only the NEXT dep change recomputes. equals:false and interposed tracked reads do NOT help. VERIFIED MITIGATIONS: (1) flush() between write and dep change; (2) issue writes from an effect/renderEffect APPLY phase (compute phase already drained — nothing to swallow).
(d) ownedWrite required and honoured on the function form (component-body setOptions throws without it — D11 NOT retired by D14); APPLY-phase writes need none. Functional writes chain (second sees first's pending result). HAZARD: a functional write after an un-flushed dep change sees the STALE pre-change prev AND swallows the change.
(e) Full memo duality: observers see every committed change from either cause; same-tick write+dep delivers ONE notification (the written value); auto-settles on microtask.
DECISION: D14 SUPERSEDES D13 — in CORRECTED form only. Delete the Solid-1 createComputed push-sync outright. VALIDATED RECIPE:
  createSignal(prev => mergeObjects(prev, mergedOptions()), { name: 'table/optionsStore', ownedWrite: true })
  get(): if (!getObserver()) flush(); return raw()            // getObserver guard LOAD-BEARING (tracked reads must not re-enter flush)
  set(u): flush(); const out = setRaw(u); flush(); return out // flush on BOTH sides; leading alone still swallows
Verified safe for set() from effect APPLY phase (re-entrant flush ok) and from component bodies (ownedWrite). D10 settle-on-read is REQUIRED (it is what makes D14 safe); D13 is not needed even as fallback. FALLBACK if flush-around-write batching cost bites (N setOptions per handler = N global drains; Solid 2 has no batch): route imperative writes through an effect APPLY phase (one scheduling hop). Measurement owed by 65n.6/65n.3.
NOT COVERED: transitions/optimistic lanes, SSR, creation inside a real component owner, createStore path.

title: Spike: two-arg createEffect timing, defer and sync options
description:
## Why
The observable() replacement (subscribe bridge) is built on the new mandatory split-signature createEffect(compute, effectFn, opts). Its first-run timing and the exact meaning of {defer} and {sync:true} determine whether the bridge needs manual eager first emission and whether sync mode delivers intermediate values.

## What
Spike tests answering: (a) when does the effect half first run relative to creation — never at creation, first flush, or immediately? (b) exact {defer:true} behavior (skip first invocation? what if a write lands between creation and first flush?); (c) does {sync:true} fire on EVERY intermediate write within a tick (breaking coalescing) or once per settle?

## Outcome
Confirms/refutes design D4 (deferred two-arg createEffect in nested createRoot) and D5 (manual eager first emission with emitted+Object.is dedup guard instead of relying on defer).
design: Plan refs: D4, D5, S2. Blocks reactivity.ts rewrite and the devtools hook rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Three timing questions answered with test evidence; D4/D5 confirmed or amended in this issue.
notes:
SPIKE ANSWERS (19 passing tests: create-effect-timing.spike.test.ts + effect-cleanup-return.spike.test.ts; durable copy: .claude/solid2-spikes/).
(a) Compute half: runs EXACTLY ONCE synchronously at creation. Effect half: NEVER at creation; first run at first flush — explicit flush() or the auto queueMicrotask(flush) a write arms (await Promise.resolve() delivers). Effect half runs in a WRITABLE scope (plain setter legal there, no ownedWrite); compute half/owner body writes hard-throw without ownedWrite.
(b) {defer:true} cleanly eats exactly the initial invocation (compute still runs at creation); a write landing before first flush IS delivered; both orderings byte-identical. BUT a source that never changes value delivers NOTHING EVER (same-value writes dedup'd by signal equality) => defer-based bridge can leave a subscriber permanently uninitialised.
(c) BEAD PREMISE WRONG: {sync:true} is NOT a scheduling mode in beta.29 — it is an async-shape assertion (skips the async probe; CONFIG_SYNC; .d.ts documents it as compiler-emission optimisation). Delivery byte-identical to option-less effect. NO per-write intermediate mode exists; only explicit flush()-per-write observes intermediates.
(d) Effect-half returned fn runs as cleanup before next invocation and on dispose; compute-half onCleanup same lifecycle, fires BEFORE effect-half cleanup. Nested createRoot parents to the enclosing owner; outer dispose tears down nested; double/late dispose never throws => D6 idempotent unsubscribe safe with zero extra guarding.
DECISION: D4 CONFIRMED. D5 CONFIRMED — manual eager first emission + emitted&&Object.is dedup; the guard is LOAD-BEARING (without it every subscriber receives the initial value twice). Do NOT use {defer:true} (right semantics for effects, wrong semantics for a subscribe bridge).
AMENDMENT 1 (CRITICAL — see table-65n.9): effect half MUST be a braced block returning undefined. Any other non-function return throws 'invalid cleanup value' AND PERMANENTLY HALTS the reactive system (REACTIVITY_HALTED; schedule() short-circuits forever). effect-cleanup-return.spike.test.ts must remain a ONE-test file.
AMENDMENT 2: strike the {sync:true} contingency from the design — no synchronous bridge lever exists.
NOT COVERED: transitions, EffectOptions.schedule flag, createRenderEffect timing, prod build.

title: Spike: Solid 2 pending-write semantics (staleness, functional prev, flush cost)
description:
## Why
Solid 2 defers all updates to the next microtask; reads return the last committed value until flush(). table-core does verified read-after-write inside batch (coreTablesFeature.utils.ts:51 untracked baseAtom.get() after same-batch writes; columnResizingFeature.utils.ts:222-238 two consecutive functional set(old=>...) that must see each other). The whole adapter architecture choice (Solid-native signals vs Svelte-style store bridge) hangs on these semantics.

## What
Throwaway tests in packages/solid-table/tests/spike/ against solid-js@2.0.0-beta.29 answering:
(a) after set(), is an untracked signal read stale until flush?
(b) is a memo read during the pending window recomputed or stale?
(c) does the functional setter's prev see pending (uncommitted) writes?
(d) cost of flush() with an empty queue — target O(1), no allocation (gates the settle-on-imperative-read design D10-A, since tableMemo reads table.options on every call)
(e) is nested flush() (flush during flush) a no-op or a throw?

## Outcome
Records the A1-vs-A2 architecture decision (D3): keep Solid-native signal atoms, or fall back to the Svelte-style store bridge (wrapExternalAtoms:false) if the graph is frozen-until-flush. Keep the spike file as a PERMANENT semantics-contract test so a Solid beta bump fails loudly.
design: Plan refs: D3, D7, D10, S1a-e. Blocks the reactivity.ts rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: All five questions answered with runnable test evidence; A1-vs-A2 decision recorded in this issue; spike file preserved as permanent contract test on the solid-2 branch.
notes:
SPIKE ANSWERS (solid-js@2.0.0-beta.29 dev runtime; 33 passing tests in pending-write-semantics.spike.test.ts; durable copy: .claude/solid2-spikes/ in repo dir; runnable copy: session scratch project w/ vitest resolve.conditions ['browser','development'] + server.deps.inline — the node condition resolves an INERT server build).
(a) YES stale: plain reads AND untrack() reads return last COMMITTED value until flush(). untrack is NOT a settle. flush(fn) does NOT settle before fn runs (drain happens after fn returns). latest(()=>s()) reads the PENDING value synchronously without draining; isPending() reports the window.
(b) OWNED and OBSERVED memos: stale until flush. UNOWNED already-computed memos: TEARING — recompute eagerly against pending source while the source signal still reads committed, same synchronous instant, read-order independent; chains propagate. => derived atoms MUST be created under the table owner or A1 ships a tearing bug.
(c) YES: functional setter prev IS pending-aware (two set(v=>v+1) commit +2; columnResizingFeature two-write mirror preserves the first write's result BY IDENTITY). Holds under ownedWrite:true inside owned scopes. Asymmetry: prev sees pending, reads do not.
(d) empty flush() ~11-12ns/op, O(1) in graph size (flat across empty graph, 100sig+100memo, 200-deep chain). Settling read = bare untracked read + ~10ns. latest() ~460ns (~8x). D10-A cost cleared decisively. Bench needs SPIKE_BENCH_LOG=1 to print ns/op.
(e) nested flush() = silent no-op (never throws, commits NOTHING) inside effect callbacks and compute halves => flush-based settle helper is INERT inside reactive scopes (acceptable: computes already read pending; use latest() if an effect must read back its own write). flush() drains GLOBALLY.
(f) ONE awaited microtask fully auto-settles (write itself arms queueMicrotask(flush)); staleness window = exactly the synchronous tick of the write. Pre-queued microtasks still see stale.
DECISION D3: A1 — KEEP Solid-native signal atoms; A2 store bridge not needed ((c), the hard gate, passes). D7 GO unconditionally. D10-A promoted to MANDATORY: imperative reads = flush(); untrack(get), guarded by getObserver(). D11 required (dev hard-throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE).
NOT COVERED: createStore/createProjection semantics, transitions/optimistic lanes, prod-build behavior.

title: Guard two-arg createEffect effect-half return values (typed emit wrapper + lint rule)
description:
## Why
table-rcv.2 spike found an app-killing footgun in solid-js@2.0.0-beta.29: the effect half's return value is a cleanup slot with a strict dev guard — returning any non-undefined non-function value (e.g. the number from arr.push(v), or any expression-bodied arrow `v => listener(v)`) throws 'effect callback returned an invalid cleanup value' AND permanently halts the entire reactive system (REACTIVITY_HALTED: schedule() short-circuits forever; every subsequent reactive op in the module is dead). Trivial to hit when forwarding subscriber callbacks whose return type is unknown.

## What
After 65n.2 lands: (a) ensure every adapter-internal effect half is a braced block returning undefined, with the observerToCallback/emit wrapper typed (v: T) => void so user subscriber return values can never leak into the cleanup slot; (b) add an eslint restriction (no expression-bodied arrow as createEffect arg 2 in solid-table src) or a wrapper helper enforced by review; (c) port the one-test spike file effect-cleanup-return.spike.test.ts as the permanent regression test (MUST stay a single-test file — the halt poisons the module for later tests).

title: Adopt flatMerge in solid-table options-sync loop (eager-resolution restructure + granularity benchmark)
description:
## Why
65n.1 vendored flatMerge (unit-tested: 200 successive merges give mergeObjects a 200-getter-hop read chain, flatMerge a plain data property) but deliberately did NOT adopt it at createTable.ts sites 76 (mergeOptions binding) and 102 (options-sync loop). Reason: in Solid the merge laziness is load-bearing — the sync computation only tracks tableOptions.state keys, and row-model memos subscribe to caller signals through the live getter chain at point of read. Flattening inside untrack freezes that snapshot, so adoption requires ALSO restructuring the computation to resolve every option getter eagerly outside untrack (svelte $effect.pre pattern, cf. svelte PR #6266). That restructure silently coarsens reactivity granularity: the options store then invalidates on every option change, so every memo reading table.options recomputes where previously only readers of the changed key did. No existing test can detect that regression.

## What
After the 65n.3 rewrite lands (which may make this moot or easy — the D14 writable-memo store changes the sync shape entirely), adopt flatMerge in the sync path WITH (a) the eager-resolution restructure and (b) a reactivity-granularity benchmark proving per-key invalidation is preserved or the coarsening is acceptable. A variant was implemented and passed all 22 pre-existing tests during 65n.1 — the mechanics are known; the benchmark is the missing piece.
